body.estimand_functional: \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}],\quad\widehat U^{\mathrm I}=\operatorname{left}_r(\mathcal P_r(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}})),\quad\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)=O_P(b_{nm})\)

sampling_model.design: A triangular array of sequential randomized decisions ordered globally by \(o(i,j)=(i-1)m+j\), with filtration \((\mathbb G_k)_{k=0}^{nm}\) and explicit row baselines \(\mathcal F_{i,0}=\mathbb G_{(i-1)m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) units observed at \(m\) ordered decision times, with bounded aspect ratio; the sharp experiment and Markov witness use \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A_{ij}\) is drawn with \(p_{ij}\in[q,1-q]\) given the global pre-cell field \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW-SVD uses known propensities. The newly defined blind procedure uses a clipped row fraction; its tangent gap is derived from the primitive oracle gap and propensity-path stability and is included in \(\rho_{nm}\). The observable discrepancy \(\widehat\rho_{nm}\) compares blind and recorded fits and diagnoses frontier-rate validity. Only the simultaneous-inference branch assumes nonsaturated rank and effective-dimension growth; it uses leave-one-cell-out rank \(r\) residuals whose uniform covariance consistency and positive studentizers are derived rather than assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Published Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, gives the rowwise upper bound, and Theorem 2, equation (22b) on page 953, gives the minimax lower bound under independent Bernoulli observation and independent noise.
Published Theorem 2.2 on page 1974 gives a Frobenius online-SGD rate and Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 gives fixed-form asymptotic normality for scalar rewards from independent Gaussian matrix contexts.
Published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 bound nearest-neighbor error for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean under an adaptive pooled sequential policy.

Published Theorem 2 and equation (14) on page 1724 give a Frobenius RMSE upper bound for nuclear-norm completion of an untreated potential-outcome matrix when adoption dates are independent across units conditional on the latent matrix.

Published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 gives a restricted-strong-convexity and Frobenius-error guarantee for the low-rank term estimated by the weighted MAR objective in equations (2) and (11).
Published Propositions 1--3 develop tall-wide factor imputation rates and limit laws for missing common components, with average and individual treatment effects on the treated as applications.

The published COLT extended abstract on pages 3821--3822 and its public full version give entrywise consistency and asymptotic normality for synthetic nearest neighbors under causal missing-not-at-random sampling.

Published Theorem 5 on page 2021 compares Frobenius upper bounds for known-propensity IPW and uniform-risk nuclear-norm completion under independent Bernoulli observation with a low-rank probability matrix.
The published article and its public full version develop groupwise nuclear-norm completion and debiased asymptotic normality for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random causal panels.

Public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 give a rowwise \(\ell_2\) treatment-effect-matrix upper bound for Algorithm 1, an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignments and low-rank arm means.
Published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 characterize variance improvement for a scalar adaptively normalized IPW estimator under independent treatment indicators.
Predictably weighted adaptive IPW scores yield scalar studentized martingale limits.
Balancing weights attain Frobenius guarantees and a lower bound under fixed heterogeneous missingness.
Debiased low-rank projection yields inference for a fixed linear form under independent sampling.

ArXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 gives normalized third-moment, predictable-covariance, empirical-covariance, plug-in, growth, and variance-floor conditions under which Theorem 3.3 on page 8 validates simultaneous multiplier intervals for many martingale means.
Published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 validate a multiplier maximum for a coefficient matrix under modeled nonuniform missingness.

body.tldr: Under an explicit row-major global filtration, recorded propensities turn the effect score into a bounded matrix martingale, and the normalized maximum-row frontier is \(b_{nm}=1\wedge[(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm})\sqrt{\log(en)}\,K r^{3/2}\mu q^{-1/2}\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}]\). IPW-SVD attains this rate under history-predictable assignments and a constant-propensity submodel gives the observed-data-measurable converse. Mehrotra et al. attain the same geometric rowwise matrix-error scale under independent assignments with low-rank arm means; the field-level advance here is the recorded-predictable effect-subspace frontier, weaker armwise structure, and matched converse. Athey et al.'s causal-panel completion and Sun et al.'s longitudinal MAR weighted completion target outcome imputation in Frobenius loss and neither imply nor are implied by this effect-subspace result. For the newly defined blind row-fraction SVD, a primitive oracle gap and propensity-path stability imply the random tangent gap; validity holds exactly when total drift \(\rho_{nm}\) is at most \(b_{nm}\), and the observed fit discrepancy \(\widehat\rho_{nm}\) diagnoses that boundary. A bounded-aspect rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is a boundary example for this new blind procedure. Under a theorem-specific nonsaturation margin, leave-one-cell-out residuals yield simultaneous dense-query bands with a separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) cost.

project_justification.gap: Mehrotra et al. establish the geometric rowwise matrix-error scale for an armwise row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignments, but not an effect-subspace theorem under history-predictable assignment or a minimax converse over estimators observing recorded propensities. Cai et al.'s independent-entry subspace bounds, Han et al.'s online matrix-context regression, Dwivedi et al.'s adaptive nearest-neighbor arm-mean inference, Athey et al.'s causal-panel Frobenius completion, and Sun et al.'s longitudinal MAR weighted completion do not fill that joint gap. Khan and Ugander's scalar affine normalization does not analyze the new row-fraction SVD or supply an observed spectral drift diagnostic.
project_justification.niche: The field-level niche is a calibrated causal row-subspace frontier that separates predictable-assignment noise, oracle path distortion, empirical-denominator tangency, observable fit disagreement, and simultaneous-query entropy.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a maximum-row upper rate and measurable-estimator converse, proves the primitive-gap-to-tangent-gap transfer, calibrates the observable blind-versus-recorded discrepancy, gives an iff frontier and a bounded-aspect boundary example for the newly defined blind procedure, and derives Belloni--Oliveira increment and covariance conditions plus uniformly positive leave-one-cell-out studentizers for a direct-IPW multiplier band with a separate family-size factor.

body.related_work: Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis are the closest rate comparator: public Algorithm 1, Theorem 3.2, and Corollary 3.3 in Section 3 give an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD and the same geometric rowwise matrix-error scale under independent Bernoulli assignments, unknown propensities, and low-rankness of each arm mean. Their result informs the geometric term but does not allow treatment probabilities to depend on recorded history, does not permit high-rank arm means whose difference is low rank, does not target the effect matrix's left singular space, and gives no minimax converse. Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen impose independent Bernoulli entry sampling and independent noise in published Assumptions 1--2 on page 948; their diagonal-deleted Gram estimator has an \(\ell_{2,\infty}\) upper bound in Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, and an independent-Gaussian minimax lower bound in Theorem 2, equation (22b) on page 953. ArXiv v5 pages 5, 7, and 10 corroborate those published locators; these results inform the perturbation and packing but do not cover a causal predictable IPW score. Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi define the untreated-potential-outcome completion problem on pages 1717--1718, impose independent noise and adoption dates in published Assumptions 1--2 on pages 1720 and 1724, and prove a nuclear-norm Frobenius RMSE bound in Theorem 2, equation (14), on page 1724. Their theorem does not imply the present result because it targets the control-outcome matrix and treatment effects on treated cells rather than the effect row subspace under within-unit predictable randomization; conversely, low rank of \(M=\mu^1-\mu^0\) does not imply low rank or estimability of their untreated matrix, so the present result gives neither their imputation bound nor their treatment-on-treated estimand. Sun, Zhu, and Dubin define the longitudinal outcome decomposition in published equation (1) and MAR propensity in Assumption 2 of Section 2, the weighted nuclear-norm objectives in equations (2) and (10)--(11) of Section 3, and the low-rank Frobenius bound in Theorem 3 of Section 4 of article e70002. Their result does not imply predictable-treatment effect-subspace recovery because its mask is MAR response missingness and its loss is Frobenius error for an outcome low-rank term; conversely, the present low-rank effect assumption supplies neither their covariate decomposition nor low-rank outcome term, and therefore does not imply their completion guarantee. Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah use the exogenous factor model in published equation (4) on page 2383 and nearest neighbors for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean in Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389; Assumption 6 on page 2397 and Theorem 4.1 on page 2398 delimit their Lipschitz factor class, which \(\mathrm{thm:dwivedi\mbox{-}separation}\) separates in both directions from the present model and target. The whole-neighborhood audit also covers Bai and Ng's published Propositions 1--3 for tall-wide factor imputation and treatment effects on treated cells, Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen's COLT pages 3821--3822 and public full version for synthetic-nearest-neighbor entrywise causal completion under missing-not-at-random sampling, Choi and Yuan's published groupwise nuclear-norm and debiasing framework for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random panels, and Mao, Wong, and Chen's independent-Bernoulli low-rank missingness model and published Theorem 5 on page 2021 for Frobenius IPW completion. These adjacent results target missing outcome entries, averages, or full-matrix losses; none provides the recorded-predictable effect-subspace upper-and-lower frontier, while the present effect-only low-rank class does not imply their armwise, block-factor, or missingness-model assumptions. Han, Sun, and Zhang specify one scalar reward per independent Gaussian matrix context in published equation (1) on page 1964 and prove a Frobenius online-SGD rate in Theorem 2.2 on page 1974; Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 concerns fixed-form asymptotic normality. Tropp supplies bounded-increment matrix Freedman inequalities. Khan and Ugander's published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 analyze a scalar affine normalizer under independent treatment indicators, and their Discussion on page 18 identifies dependent indicators as an open extension; they do not define the row-fraction SVD here, so the Markov boundary example is not a refutation of their procedure. Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey justify recorded-propensity scalar martingale scores. Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan provide a fixed heterogeneous-missingness Frobenius benchmark. Xia and Yuan's published Section 1 conditions after equation (5) require loading alignment and an \(\ell_1\) size condition for their independent noisy-matrix fixed-form inference; those conditions are not cited as support for the deterministic dense loadings here. Belloni and Oliveira's arXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 states the normalized third-moment, predictable-covariance, empirical-covariance, plug-in, dimension-growth, and variance-floor hypotheses used by Theorem 3.3 on page 8; the multiplier-primitives lemma derives the non-covariance inputs and imposes their covariance stabilization directly. Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu's published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 give a multiplier maximum for modeled nonadaptive missingness. Spruijt-Metz et al. make saved propensities and sensitivity to their omission concrete in HeartSteps II.

body.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected frontier is larger than \(b^0_{nm}\). With balanced dimensions and \(\lambda_{nm}\asymp B\sqrt{nm}\), maximum-row noise gives \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\), not \(n^{-1/2}\). At \(\lambda_{nm}\asymp B\sqrt{n\log n}\), normalized maximum-row loss can remain constant. The primitive class restricts only the effect matrix: the denominator derivative \(H^{\mathrm B}\) contains the separate arm means, and no primitive condition in this core supplies a frontier-rate estimator of those means from one realized arm per cell. Accordingly, the blind branch retains the implementable fit-disagreement certificate and does not assert a tangent correction. The simultaneous-band theorem excludes \(r=\min(n,m)\), because any rank \(r\) projection then interpolates the score and destroys residual studentization; this exclusion does not affect the rate, converse, or blind frontier. Sharp dependence on growing \(r\), \(\mu\), and \(K\) remains in the sharp-constant question.
body.honest_scope: Identification and the fixed-propensity algebra are reductions. Maximum-row martingale perturbation, the matched packing, the primitive-gap transfer, the ratio remainder, calibration of the observed discrepancy, Markov concentration, leave-one-cell-out covariance consistency, and multiplier approximation are to be established. Mehrotra et al. settle the analogous geometric rowwise matrix-error upper scale under independent assignments and armwise low rank; the open contribution here begins at predictable assignment, effect-subspace loss, effect-only low rank, and the matched converse. The blind row-fraction SVD is introduced in this core; the Markov sequence is its boundary example and makes no claim about a published procedure. Constant propensities make the oracle blind center equal \(M\) but do not erase the empirical-denominator tangent. The diagnostic is sharp only up to the \(b_{nm}\) stochastic resolution, so local alternatives inside that boundary are not distinguishable. No denominator-tangent correction is claimed because the existing primitives do not impose estimable structure on the separate arm means entering \(H^{\mathrm B}\). Cross-fitting is used only to construct residuals; its consistency follows from martingale concentration and low-rank approximation, not from an independence assertion. The sharp minimax constant is posed only along the explicit bounded-aspect path and only over estimators measurable from \(A\), \(Y\), and \(p\).
